question: Why can repeatedly calling add() on this class eventually cause a memory problem, even though Java has automatic garbage collection?
options: Because the objects are still reachable through the static cache list, so the garbage collector cannot reclaim them even if nothing else references them
Because Java cannot garbage collect static fields at all
Because ArrayList has a hard-coded maximum size of 10
Because add() copies each object twice
explanation: Garbage collection only reclaims objects that are unreachable. Since cache is static and keeps growing, every added object remains reachable through it, preventing collection and causing unbounded memory growth — a classic memory leak despite GC.
